text: The Indian Parliament consists of:
options: Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and the President
Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha only
explanation: The Union Parliament comprises the President and two Houses: the Lok Sabha (House of the People) and the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).

text: The minimum age to become a member of the Lok Sabha is:
explanation: The minimum age to be elected to the Lok Sabha (Lower House) is 25 years. For Rajya Sabha, the minimum age is 30 years.

text: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is:
explanation: The Constitution provides for a maximum of 552 seats in Lok Sabha: up to 530 from states, up to 20 from UTs, and 2 nominated from Anglo-Indian community (latter abolished in 2019).

text: A Money Bill can originate in:
explanation: Money Bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha (Article 110). The Rajya Sabha can suggest amendments but cannot reject Money Bills.

text: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House because:
options: It is never dissolved; one-third of members retire every 2 years
The President is a permanent member
explanation: Rajya Sabha (Upper House) is a permanent body — it cannot be dissolved. One-third of its members retire every two years and are replaced by fresh elections.

text: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is elected by:
explanation: The Speaker is elected from among the members of the Lok Sabha by the members themselves. The Speaker presides over Lok Sabha sittings.

text: The Prime Minister of India is appointed by:
explanation: The Prime Minister is appointed by the President under Article 75. Conventionally, the leader of the party commanding majority in Lok Sabha is appointed PM.

text: The Prime Minister holds office:
options: As long as they command majority in Lok Sabha
At the pleasure of the President alone
explanation: The PM holds office so long as they enjoy the confidence (majority) of the Lok Sabha. If the PM loses a vote of no confidence, they must resign.

text: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to:
explanation: Under Article 75(3), the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (House of the People). If the Lok Sabha passes a no-confidence motion, the entire cabinet must resign.

text: The Prime Minister advises the President on:
options: Appointment of governors, judges, and constitutional authorities
explanation: The PM advises the President on all major appointments: governors, ambassadors, judges of High and Supreme Courts, and heads of constitutional bodies (like CAG, Election Commission).

text: The President of India is elected by:
options: An electoral college (elected MPs and MLAs)
explanation: The President is elected by an Electoral College comprising elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of State Legislative Assemblies (Article 54).

text: The term of office of the President of India is:
explanation: The President holds office for 5 years from the date of entering office. They are eligible for re-election.

text: The President of India can be removed by:
options: Vote of no confidence in Lok Sabha
explanation: The President can be removed by impeachment — a resolution passed by special majority in either House and agreed by the other House (Article 61).

text: The power of the President to dissolve the Lok Sabha is exercised:
options: On the advice of the Prime Minister
On the advice of the Speaker
On the advice of Rajya Sabha
explanation: The President can dissolve the Lok Sabha only on the advice of the Prime Minister (Article 85). The President is a constitutional head and acts on ministerial advice.

text: The President's Ordinance-making power (Article 123) can be used when:
options: Parliament is not in session and immediate action is needed
Any time at the President's discretion
explanation: The President can promulgate Ordinances when Parliament is not in session and an immediate legislative requirement arises. Ordinances have the same force as Acts but must be placed before Parliament when it reassembles.

text: The Chief Justice of India is appointed by:
explanation: The Chief Justice of India (CJI) is appointed by the President of India, by convention following the seniority principle (the most senior judge of the Supreme Court is appointed).

text: The Supreme Court of India is located in:
explanation: The Supreme Court of India, the highest court in the land, is located in New Delhi.

text: Original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court means it can:
options: Hear disputes between the Centre and States directly
explanation: Article 131: The Supreme Court has exclusive original jurisdiction over disputes between the Centre and States or between States, which no other court can entertain.

text: Writ of Habeas Corpus means:
options: 'You may have the body' — to produce the detained person before court
'We Command' — to compel a public official to do their duty
explanation: Habeas Corpus (Latin: 'have the body') is a writ directing a detaining authority to produce the detained person before court to determine legality of detention — a fundamental safeguard of personal liberty.

text: Judicial review power of the Supreme Court means it can:
options: Declare laws unconstitutional if they violate the Constitution
explanation: Judicial review allows the Supreme Court to examine legislation and executive actions and strike them down if they violate the Constitution (especially Fundamental Rights).

text: The Indian National Congress was founded in:
explanation: The Indian National Congress (INC) was founded in December 1885 by Allan Octavian Hume with 72 delegates meeting in Bombay (Mumbai).

text: The first session of the Indian National Congress was presided over by:
explanation: Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee presided over the first session of the INC in 1885, held in Bombay.

text: The partition of Bengal in 1905 was announced by:
explanation: Lord Curzon (Viceroy) partitioned Bengal in 1905 into East Bengal (with Assam) and West Bengal, ostensibly for administrative reasons but actually to divide the nationalist movement.

text: The Swadeshi Movement was launched as a response to:
explanation: The Swadeshi Movement was launched in 1905 in protest against the Partition of Bengal. It involved boycott of British goods and promotion of Indian manufactures.

text: The Moderates of the Indian National Congress advocated:
options: Constitutional means, petitions, and prayers to British government
explanation: Early INC leaders (Moderates like Gokhale, Naoroji) believed in constitutional agitation — petitions, resolutions, press campaigns — trusting British sense of justice to grant reforms.

text: The First World War lasted from:
explanation: World War I (the Great War) was fought from 28 July 1914 to 11 November 1918.

text: The assassination of which Archduke triggered WWI?
explanation: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria-Hungary in Sarajevo on 28 June 1914 by Gavrilo Princip (a Bosnian Serb) triggered WWI.

text: The Allied Powers in WWI included:
explanation: Allied Powers (Triple Entente): Britain, France, Russia; Italy (switched sides); USA (joined 1917). Central Powers: Germany, Austria-Hungary, Ottoman Empire, Bulgaria.

text: The Treaty of Versailles (1919) imposed:
options: Heavy reparations on Germany and the war-guilt clause
Creation of the League of Nations only
Allowed Germany to keep all territories
explanation: The Treaty of Versailles imposed the 'war guilt clause' (Article 231), required Germany to pay reparations (132 billion gold marks), stripped Germany of colonies and territories, and limited its army.

text: New military technology used for the first time in WWI included:
options: Poison gas, tanks, aircraft, and submarines
explanation: WWI saw the first large-scale use of: poison gas (chlorine, mustard gas), tanks (by Britain in 1916), military aircraft (reconnaissance and bombing), and submarines (German U-boats).

text: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was between:
options: Indian National Congress and Muslim League
explanation: The Lucknow Pact (1916) was a significant agreement between the INC (led by Tilak) and the Muslim League (led by Jinnah) for Hindu-Muslim unity and joint demands for constitutional reforms.

text: The Russian Revolution of 1917 led to the overthrow of:
options: Tsar Nicholas II and the establishment of a communist state
explanation: The 1917 Russian Revolution ended the Romanov dynasty (Tsar Nicholas II abdicated) and, through the Bolshevik Revolution, led to the world's first communist state.

text: The leader of the Bolshevik party in the Russian Revolution was:
explanation: Vladimir Ilyich Lenin led the Bolshevik party which overthrew the Provisional Government in October 1917, establishing Soviet power in Russia.

text: The ideology of the Bolsheviks was based on:
options: Marxism (class struggle and abolition of private property)
explanation: The Bolsheviks were Marxist revolutionaries who believed in the proletariat's (working class) overthrow of capitalism, state ownership of means of production, and a classless communist society.

text: The New Economic Policy (NEP) introduced by Lenin in 1921 was:
options: A partial return to market economy to revive Russia after civil war
explanation: After the devastating civil war and War Communism, Lenin's NEP (1921) allowed limited private enterprise in agriculture and small industry to revive the collapsed economy — a pragmatic tactical retreat.

text: Adolf Hitler's political party in Germany was the:
options: National Socialist German Workers' Party (NSDAP/Nazi Party)
explanation: Hitler led the National Socialist German Workers' Party (Nationalsozialistische Deutsche Arbeiterpartei — NSDAP), known as the Nazi Party, which came to power in 1933.

text: Benito Mussolini led which country as dictator?
explanation: Benito Mussolini was the fascist dictator of Italy (1922–1943). He founded the National Fascist Party and his movement gave the world the term 'fascism'.

text: The Great Depression of 1929 contributed to the rise of dictatorships because:
options: Economic crisis created mass unemployment, despair, and receptiveness to extremist solutions
explanation: The Great Depression caused massive unemployment, hyperinflation, and social unrest, undermining faith in democratic governments and making people susceptible to the promises of fascist and Nazi movements.

text: The policy of Appeasement towards Hitler (as at Munich, 1938) was pursued primarily by:
explanation: Britain (Chamberlain) and France (Daladier) pursued appeasement — giving in to Hitler's demands (e.g., allowing annexation of Sudetenland at Munich 1938) to avoid war.

text: World War II began in:
explanation: World War II began on 1 September 1939 when Germany invaded Poland. Britain and France declared war on Germany on 3 September 1939.

text: The Allied Powers in WWII included:
options: Britain, France, USA, USSR, and others
explanation: Allied Powers in WWII: Britain, France, USA (after Pearl Harbor 1941), USSR (after Germany's invasion 1941), China. Axis Powers: Germany, Italy, Japan.

text: The first atomic bombs were dropped on:
explanation: The USA dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima (6 August 1945) and Nagasaki (9 August 1945), forcing Japan's surrender and ending WWII.

text: Operation Barbarossa (June 1941) refers to:
options: Germany's invasion of the Soviet Union
explanation: Operation Barbarossa was Nazi Germany's massive invasion of the Soviet Union (22 June 1941) — the largest military operation in history — which eventually turned the tide of the war against Germany.

text: The Non-Cooperation Movement of 1920–22 was launched by:
explanation: Mahatma Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920, calling on Indians to boycott British institutions, goods, schools, and courts. It was suspended after Chauri Chaura violence in 1922.

text: The Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha) was conducted in:
explanation: Gandhi led the Dandi March from 12 March to 6 April 1930, walking 241 miles to Dandi (Gujarat) to break the British salt laws by making salt from seawater — a key event of the Civil Disobedience Movement.

text: The Quit India Movement of 1942 was launched with the slogan:
options: 'Do or Die' — demanding immediate British withdrawal
explanation: Gandhi launched the Quit India Movement on 8 August 1942 with the slogan 'Do or Die', demanding immediate British withdrawal from India. It led to massive arrests and repression.

text: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred on:
explanation: On 13 April 1919 (Baisakhi), General Dyer ordered troops to fire on an unarmed crowd at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar, killing hundreds. It shocked the nation and intensified the freedom struggle.

text: The Cabinet Mission Plan (1946) proposed:
options: A federal united India with provinces grouped into three sections
explanation: The Cabinet Mission Plan (1946) proposed keeping India united with a loose confederation — provinces grouped into three sections (A: Hindu majority, B & C: Muslim majority). INC and Muslim League disagreed on interpretation, leading to partition.

text: The writ of Mandamus is issued to:
options: Compel a public official or body to perform their legal duty
Prohibit lower court from exceeding jurisdiction
explanation: Mandamus (Latin: 'we command') is a writ issued by a superior court ordering a public authority, lower court, corporation, or government to perform a public or statutory duty they have wrongly refused.

text: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992) relates to:
explanation: The 73rd Amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions — the three-tier system of rural local self-government: Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, Zila Parishad.

text: The Home Rule Movement (1916) was launched by:
options: Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant separately
explanation: Two Home Rule Leagues were established in 1916: one by Tilak (April) centred in Maharashtra, and another by Annie Besant (September) centred in Madras. Both demanded self-government within the British Empire.

text: D-Day (Operation Overlord) refers to:
options: Allied invasion of Normandy, France on 6 June 1944
explanation: D-Day (6 June 1944): Allied forces (American, British, Canadian) landed on the beaches of Normandy, France — the largest seaborne invasion in history — opening a Western Front that led to Germany's defeat.

text: A joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament is presided over by:
explanation: A joint sitting of Parliament (held to resolve disagreement between Houses on ordinary legislation) is presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha (Article 108).

text: Who performs the function of President in the absence of both the President and Vice-President?
explanation: If both the President and Vice-President are unavailable, the Chief Justice of India acts as President of India.

text: The famous slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright' was given by:
explanation: 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it' is the famous declaration by Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Lokmanya), emphasising the right of Indians to self-rule.

text: India gained independence on:
explanation: India became independent on 15 August 1947. The Constitution came into effect on 26 January 1950, marking India becoming a Republic.

text: The Supreme Court of India has how many judges (including the CJI)?
explanation: The Supreme Court of India currently has a sanctioned strength of 34 judges (including the Chief Justice). The original Constitution provided for 8 judges; Parliament has increased this over time.

text: The Soviet Union (USSR) was formally established in:
explanation: The Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR) was formally established on 30 December 1922, uniting Russia, Ukraine, Byelorussia, and Transcaucasia.

text: The Night of the Long Knives (1934) was Hitler's move to:
options: Eliminate rivals within the Nazi Party (especially SA/Stormtroopers)
explanation: The Night of the Long Knives (30 June–2 July 1934): Hitler had Ernst Röhm and SA leaders murdered to appease the Army and consolidate absolute power, removing any potential internal opposition.

text: The 74th Constitutional Amendment (1992) relates to:
explanation: The 74th Amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to Urban Local Bodies: Nagar Panchayats, Municipal Councils, and Municipal Corporations, providing for regular elections and reserved seats.

text: Under Article 368, constitutional amendments can be passed by:
options: Special majority (2/3 of members present and voting + majority of total membership) in each House
explanation: Most constitutional amendments require a special majority: passed by 2/3 of members present and voting AND absolute majority (50%+1 of total membership) in each House separately, under Article 368.

text: The Schlieffen Plan was Germany's strategy in WWI to:
options: Attack France quickly through Belgium, then turn to face Russia
Use naval power to blockade Britain
explanation: The Schlieffen Plan aimed for a quick defeat of France (6 weeks) through Belgium while holding Russia, then transfer troops east to face the slower-mobilising Russian army. It failed due to Belgian resistance and British entry.

text: The Simon Commission (1927) was opposed because:
explanation: The Simon Commission (7 British MPs to review the Constitution) was boycotted and opposed with black flags and 'Simon Go Back' protests because it had no Indian members.

text: The Prime Minister's authority over the Council of Ministers includes:
options: Presiding over Cabinet meetings, coordinating departments, recommending appointments to President
explanation: The PM is the 'primus inter pares' (first among equals) — presides over Cabinet, coordinates policy, advises President on ministerial appointments, and can recommend dismissal of a minister.

text: The Rowlatt Act (1919) was opposed because it:
options: Allowed detention without trial, suppressing political activity
explanation: The Rowlatt Act (Black Act) allowed the government to imprison suspects without trial for up to 2 years. It outraged Indians and triggered Gandhi's first all-India satyagraha.

text: The Holocaust during WWII refers to:
options: Systematic genocide of 6 million Jews by the Nazis
explanation: The Holocaust was the state-sponsored systematic persecution and murder of approximately 6 million Jews (and others) by the Nazi regime and its collaborators between 1941 and 1945.

text: Subhas Chandra Bose formed the Indian National Army (INA) with the slogan:
explanation: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose led the INA (Azad Hind Fauj) with patriotic slogans 'Jai Hind' (Victory to India) and 'Delhi Chalo' (March to Delhi) — fighting with Japanese against British forces.

text: Certiorari is a writ issued to:
options: Quash the order of a lower court/tribunal that exceeded its jurisdiction
Compel a public authority to act
Transfer a case from one court to another
explanation: Certiorari ('to be made certain'): superior court orders a lower court/tribunal to send records for review, and may quash the lower court's order if it was given without jurisdiction or in error of law.

text: The Khilafat Movement was launched to:
options: Protest against the dismemberment of the Ottoman Caliphate after WWI
explanation: The Khilafat Movement (1919–22) was led by Ali brothers (Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali) to protect the Ottoman Caliph's position. Gandhi supported it to build Hindu-Muslim unity during the Non-Cooperation Movement.

text: The Gram Sabha is the:
options: General assembly of all voters in a village panchayat area
explanation: Gram Sabha consists of all registered voters in a Gram Panchayat area. It is the foundation of democratic decentralisation — the most basic unit of local self-government.

text: Article 356 (President's Rule) can be imposed on a state when:
options: Constitutional machinery fails in a state (on Governor's or PM's advice)
explanation: President's Rule (Article 356) is imposed when the constitutional machinery in a state fails — the state government cannot function in accordance with the Constitution. It requires parliamentary approval.

text: The United Nations Organisation was established in:
explanation: The United Nations was established on 24 October 1945 (UN Day) after WWII, replacing the failed League of Nations, with the Charter signed by 51 founding member states.

text: Stalin's collectivisation policy in the 1930s forced:
options: Peasants to give up private farms and join collective (kolkhoz) and state farms (sovkhoz)
Farmers to produce only cash crops
City workers to move to farms
explanation: Stalin's forced collectivisation (1929–33) transferred ownership of farmland from private peasants to collective farms (kolkhozy). It caused massive famines, notably the Holodomor in Ukraine, killing millions.

text: The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of:
explanation: Under Article 64, the Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).

text: The Cripps Mission of 1942 was rejected by the INC because:
options: It offered Dominion status only after WWII, not immediate independence, and allowed provinces/states to opt out
It gave full power to the army
It was a Muslim League proposal
explanation: Cripps Mission promised Dominion status only after war, a Constituent Assembly, and the right of provinces to opt out (which Gandhi called 'a post-dated cheque on a failing bank'). INC rejected it as inadequate.

text: USA entered WWI in:
explanation: USA entered WWI in April 1917, triggered by German unrestricted submarine warfare (sinking American ships) and the Zimmermann Telegram (Germany's offer to Mexico to attack the USA).

text: The Nuremberg Laws (1935) in Nazi Germany:
options: Stripped Jews of citizenship and banned marriage with non-Jews
Required Jews to serve in the army
explanation: The Nuremberg Laws (September 1935) revoked Jewish citizenship, banned marriage or sexual relations between Jews and non-Jewish Germans, and excluded Jews from public office — a key step in persecution.

text: The Commissioner (Municipal Commissioner) of a Municipal Corporation is:
options: An IAS officer appointed by state government who heads administration
explanation: The Municipal Commissioner (an IAS officer) is appointed by the state government and is the chief executive of a Municipal Corporation, responsible for day-to-day administration.

text: The Supreme Court's advisory jurisdiction (Article 143) allows the President to:
options: Refer questions of law or fact of public importance to SC for its opinion
Direct the SC to hear a case
explanation: Under Article 143, the President may refer any question of law or fact of public importance to the Supreme Court for its advisory opinion. The SC may refuse and its opinion is not binding.

text: The famous 'Tryst with Destiny' speech on 14–15 August 1947 was delivered by:
explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru delivered the famous 'Tryst with Destiny' speech to the Constituent Assembly on the midnight of 14–15 August 1947, marking India's independence.

text: Pearl Harbor was attacked by:
explanation: Japan launched a surprise attack on the US naval base at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii, on 7 December 1941 ('a date which will live in infamy'), bringing the USA into WWII.

text: The League of Nations was proposed by:
options: US President Woodrow Wilson (in his 14 Points)
explanation: US President Wilson proposed the League of Nations in his Fourteen Points (January 1918). Ironically, the US Senate refused to ratify the Treaty of Versailles and the USA never joined the League.

text: Gandhiji's philosophy of non-violent resistance is known as:
explanation: Satyagraha ('truth-force' or 'soul-force') is Gandhi's philosophy and practice of non-violent resistance to injustice — used in South Africa and India's freedom struggle.

text: The Bolsheviks took power in Russia in the _____ Revolution of 1917.
explanation: The Bolshevik seizure of power occurred in the October Revolution (7 November 1917 in the Gregorian calendar / 25 October Old Style), overthrowing the Provisional Government.

text: The system of 'Dyarchy' introduced by the Government of India Act 1919 meant:
options: Division of subjects between reserved (British) and transferred (Indian ministers)
explanation: Dyarchy: provincial subjects divided into 'reserved' (law, order, finance — controlled by British) and 'transferred' (education, public health — controlled by elected Indian ministers). A step towards responsible government.

text: The Prime Minister is the head of:
explanation: The Prime Minister is the head of the Cabinet (Union Council of Ministers) and is the most powerful executive authority, though the President is the Constitutional head of state.

text: The Axis Powers in WWII comprised:
explanation: The three main Axis Powers were Nazi Germany, Fascist Italy, and Imperial Japan, united by the Tripartite Pact (1940).

text: Prohibition is a writ that:
options: Prevents a lower court from proceeding with a case outside its jurisdiction
explanation: Prohibition (or Writ of Prohibition) is issued by a superior court to prevent a lower court or tribunal from proceeding with a case in excess of its jurisdiction.

text: 'Vande Mataram', the national song of India, was written by:
explanation: Vande Mataram was written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay and appeared in his novel Anandamath (1882). The first two stanzas were adopted as the national song.

text: The Round Table Conferences (1930–32) were convened to:
options: Discuss constitutional reforms for India with British and Indian representatives
explanation: Three Round Table Conferences (1930, 1931, 1932) were held in London to discuss constitutional reforms for India. Gandhi attended the second (1931) as INC's representative. They led to the Government of India Act 1935.

text: The immediate cause of the February 1917 Revolution in Russia was:
options: Food shortages, military defeats in WWI, and worker strikes in Petrograd
explanation: The February Revolution was caused by bread shortages, war exhaustion, strikes, and the Tsar's inability to handle the crisis — leading to his abdication.

text: The term 'Fascism' comes from the Italian word 'fascio' meaning:
options: A bundle/group (symbol of strength through unity)
explanation: Fascism comes from 'fascio' (bundle of rods with an axe) — a Roman symbol of authority. Mussolini used it to represent strength through collective unity under authoritarian leadership.

text: A bill becomes an Act when:
options: Both Houses pass it and it receives Presidential assent
explanation: An ordinary bill becomes an Act when passed by both Houses of Parliament and receives the assent of the President (or is re-passed by Parliament overriding Presidential veto).

text: The Mayor of a Municipal Corporation is:
options: The ceremonial head elected from among the councillors
explanation: The Mayor is the elected head of a Municipal Corporation, elected by the elected councillors from among themselves. The real executive head is the Municipal Commissioner (IAS officer).

text: The Mountbatten Plan (3 June 1947) provided for:
options: Partition of India into India and Pakistan, with provinces and states choosing their dominion
A united India with federal structure
Independence under a Commonwealth arrangement only
explanation: The Mountbatten Plan (3 June Plan) provided for partition of India into two dominions — India and Pakistan — with Bengal and Punjab divided. Princely states could accede to either dominion.

text: The Triple Alliance before WWI consisted of:
explanation: The Triple Alliance (1882): Germany, Austria-Hungary, and Italy. Italy later switched sides and joined the Allies (1915). The opposing Triple Entente: Britain, France, Russia.

text: The Government of India Act 1935 introduced:
options: Provincial autonomy, dyarchy at Centre, and an All-India Federation (though federation never started)
explanation: The 1935 Act granted full provincial autonomy (elected governments in provinces), created a bicameral federal legislature, and proposed an All-India Federation (never came into force). It formed the basis for India's 1950 Constitution.

text: The Potsdam Conference (July–August 1945) involved:
options: USA (Truman), Britain (Attlee), and USSR (Stalin) discussing post-war order and ultimatum to Japan
explanation: Potsdam Conference (July 1945): USA (Truman replaced Roosevelt), Britain (Attlee replaced Churchill after UK election), USSR (Stalin) — discussed post-war Europe, German occupation, and issued the Potsdam Declaration demanding Japan's surrender.

text: The maximum gap between two sessions of Parliament cannot exceed:
explanation: Article 85: Parliament must be summoned at least twice a year with not more than 6 months between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next.

text: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel is known as the 'Iron Man of India' because of his role in:
options: Integrating 500+ princely states into the Indian Union after independence
explanation: Patel (India's first Home and Deputy PM) was instrumental in persuading or pressuring over 560 princely states to accede to the Indian Union — the greatest political integration in modern history.

text: The First War of Indian Independence (Sepoy Mutiny) took place in:
explanation: The Revolt of 1857 (First War of Independence / Sepoy Mutiny) began at Meerut on May 10, 1857. [Board 2017] 1905 = Partition of Bengal; 1885 = Indian National Congress founded; 1947 = Independence.

text: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by:
explanation: The INC was founded by Allan Octavian Hume (a retired British civil servant) along with Dadabhai Naoroji and Dinshaw Wacha in 1885. [Board 2017] Tilak was a Extremist leader; Naoroji was first president; Gokhale was a Moderate leader.

text: The Civil Disobedience Movement was launched by Gandhi in:
explanation: Gandhi launched the Civil Disobedience Movement on March 12, 1930 with the Dandi Salt March. [Board 2017] 1920 = Non-Cooperation Movement; 1942 = Quit India Movement; 1919 = Rowlatt Act/Jallianwala Bagh year.

text: The United Nations Organisation was established in:
explanation: The UN was established on October 24, 1945, after the end of World War II. [Board 2017] 1939 = WW2 start; 1919 = League of Nations formed; 1948 = Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

text: The Constitution of India came into effect on:
explanation: India became a Republic on 26 January 1950 when the Constitution came into force. [Board 2017] 15 Aug 1947 = Independence Day; 26 Nov 1949 = Constitution adopted; 26 Jan 1947 is fictitious.

text: The Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32) is called the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution by:
explanation: Dr B.R. Ambedkar called Article 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution as it allows citizens to approach Supreme Court to enforce Fundamental Rights. [Board 2017]

text: The immediate cause of World War I was:
explanation: Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria was assassinated at Sarajevo on June 28, 1914, triggering WWI. [Board 2017] Invasion of Poland = WWII; Lusitania sinking = 1915 (US involvement factor); Treaty of Versailles = end of WWI.

text: The Upper House of the Indian Parliament is called:
explanation: Rajya Sabha (Council of States) is the Upper House, Lok Sabha is Lower House of Parliament. [Board 2017] Vidhan Sabha = State Legislative Assembly; Vidhan Parishad = State Legislative Council.

text: The Non-Aligned Movement was co-founded by:
explanation: NAM was founded in 1961 by Jawaharlal Nehru (India), Gamal Abdel Nasser (Egypt) and Josip Broz Tito (Yugoslavia). [Board 2017]

text: 'Do or Die' was the slogan of:
explanation: Gandhi gave the 'Do or Die' slogan during the Quit India Movement launched on August 9, 1942. [Board 2017] Non-Cooperation (1920) had no such slogan; Civil Disobedience (1930) had 'march to make salt'; Swadeshi (1905) had boycott focus.

text: The Partition of Bengal was annulled in:
explanation: Bengal was partitioned in 1905 by Lord Curzon and the partition was annulled in 1911 (Delhi Durbar). [Board 2018] 1905 = partition announced; 1919 = Montagu-Chelmsford reforms; 1920 = NCM.

text: The Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj) was led by:
explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose (Netaji) reorganised and led the Indian National Army during WWII with the slogan 'Delhi Chalo'. [Board 2018] Bhagat Singh = revolutionary; Lala Lajpat Rai = Lal-Bal-Pal trio; Patel = Iron Man of India.

text: Under which Article can the President declare a National Emergency?
explanation: Article 352 deals with National Emergency (threat to security of India). [Board 2018] 356 = State Emergency (President's Rule); 360 = Financial Emergency; 368 = Amendment procedure.

text: The atomic bombs were dropped on Japan in:
explanation: Atomic bombs were dropped on Hiroshima (Aug 6) and Nagasaki (Aug 9), 1945, ending WWII in the Pacific. [Board 2018] May 1945 = Germany's surrender; Sept 1945 = formal Japanese surrender; June 1944 = D-Day Normandy.

text: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is:
explanation: Lok Sabha can have up to 552 members: 530 from states, 20 from UTs, 2 Anglo-Indian (now discontinued). Current elected = 543. [Board 2018] 545 = elected + nominated (pre-2020); 543 = current elected seats; 500 is wrong.

text: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was an agreement between:
options: INC and All India Hindu Mahasabha
explanation: The Lucknow Pact was between the Indian National Congress and the All India Muslim League — a milestone for Hindu-Muslim unity. [Board 2018]

text: Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in:
explanation: Directive Principles are in Part IV (Articles 36-51). Fundamental Rights are in Part III. [Board 2018] Part III = Fundamental Rights; Part II = Citizenship; Part V = The Union.

text: The Cuban Missile Crisis occurred in:
explanation: The Cuban Missile Crisis (October 1962) was the closest the Cold War came to nuclear conflict — US vs USSR over missiles in Cuba. [Board 2018] 1945 = WW2 end; 1950 = Korean War; 1970 = Nixon détente era.

text: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution begins with the words:
explanation: The Preamble begins: 'WE, THE PEOPLE OF INDIA, having solemnly resolved to constitute India into a SOVEREIGN SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC...' [Board 2018]

text: The first Non-Aligned Summit Conference was held in:
explanation: First NAM Summit was in Belgrade in 1961. Bandung Conference (1955) was a precursor but not NAM. [Board 2018] New Delhi 1983 = 7th Summit; Cairo 1964 = 2nd Summit.

text: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on:
explanation: On April 13, 1919 (Baisakhi day), General Dyer ordered firing on a peaceful gathering at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar. [Board 2019] May 10, 1857 = 1857 revolt; Aug 9, 1942 = Quit India; March 12, 1930 = Dandi March.

text: Money Bills can originate only in:
explanation: A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha (Article 110). Rajya Sabha can suggest changes but cannot reject it. [Board 2019] Rajya Sabha cannot originate money bills; not either house; joint session doesn't apply to money bills.

text: Dandi March started on March 12, 1930 from:
explanation: Gandhi started the 241-mile Dandi March from Sabarmati Ashram on March 12, 1930 with 78 followers. [Board 2019] Wardha was another of Gandhi's ashrams; Calcutta was Bengal's capital; Delhi was the imperial capital.

text: The number of permanent members of the UN Security Council is:
explanation: 5 permanent members (P5) with veto power: USA, UK, France, Russia, China. [Board 2019] 4 is wrong; 10 are non-permanent rotating members; 15 is total Security Council members.

text: The Chief Justice of India is appointed by:
explanation: The Chief Justice of India is appointed by the President of India on the recommendation of the outgoing Chief Justice (collegium system). [Board 2019]

text: The Holocaust refers to the systematic genocide of:
explanation: The Holocaust (Shoah) was the genocide of approximately 6 million Jews by the Nazi regime under Adolf Hitler during WW2. [Board 2019] Armenian genocide = WW1; Bosnian genocide = 1995; Rwanda = 1994.

text: The Moderates and Extremists finally split at the Surat Session of INC in:
explanation: The Surat Split (1907) divided INC into Moderates (led by Gokhale) and Extremists (led by Tilak). [Board 2019] 1905 = Bengal Partition; 1909 = Morley-Minto reforms; 1915 = Gandhi's return to India.

text: The Right to Education (Article 21A) was made a Fundamental Right by:
explanation: The 86th Amendment (2002) inserted Article 21A making free and compulsory education for children 6-14 years a Fundamental Right. [Board 2019] 44th: restored original fundamental rights removed by 42nd; 42nd: Emergency Amendment; 73rd: Panchayati Raj.

text: NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organisation) was formed in:
explanation: NATO was formed on April 4, 1949 as a Western military alliance against Soviet threat. [Board 2019] 1945 = UN formed; 1955 = Warsaw Pact (Soviet response to NATO); 1960 = height of Cold War but not NATO formation.

text: The Rowlatt Act (1919) was opposed because it:
explanation: The Rowlatt Act authorised the government to detain any person without trial for up to 2 years — leading to nationwide protests. [Board 2019] No direct taxation; press freedom already restricted; partition was 1947.

text: Gandhi's philosophy of Satyagraha means:
explanation: Satyagraha = 'Satya' (truth) + 'Agraha' (firmness). It is non-violent resistance based on truth and love. [Board 2020] Armed struggle = Bal Gangadhar Tilak's method; negotiation is political; boycott is one component.

text: The Constitution of India adopted on 26 November 1949 has how many Articles (originally)?
explanation: The original Constitution had 395 Articles, 8 Schedules and 22 Parts. [Board 2020] 448 = current articles (after amendments); 444 and 500 are incorrect.

text: The headquarters of the United Nations is located in:
explanation: UN Headquarters is in New York City, USA (Manhattan). [Board 2020] Geneva has UN offices (UNHCR, WHO); Vienna has IAEA; Brussels has EU/NATO HQ.

text: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body. This means:
options: It is never dissolved; 1/3 members retire every 2 years
It can stay even after elections
explanation: Rajya Sabha is permanent — it cannot be dissolved. 1/3 of its members retire every 2 years; each member serves a 6-year term. [Board 2020] Elections don't affect Rajya Sabha dissolution; members don't serve lifelong; it cannot self-dissolve.

text: D-Day (Operation Overlord) was the Allied invasion of:
explanation: D-Day (June 6, 1944) saw Allied forces land on beaches of Normandy, France — the largest seaborne invasion in history. [Board 2020] Germany was the final target; Italy was invaded earlier in 1943; Soviet Union was Allied.

text: Which Fundamental Right prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth?
explanation: Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth. [Board 2020] Article 14 = equality before law; Article 16 = equal opportunity in public employment; Article 17 = abolition of untouchability.

text: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were hanged on:
explanation: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were hanged at Lahore Central Jail on March 23, 1931. [Board 2020] March 31, 1930 is wrong; Aug 15, 1947 = Independence; Feb 14, 1929 = Lahore conspiracy case shooting.

text: The principle of Panchsheel (Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence) was signed between:
explanation: Panchsheel Agreement was signed between India and China on April 29, 1954. [Board 2020] India-Pakistan: no Panchsheel; India-USA: not a panchsheel signatory; India-USSR: Treaty of Peace and Friendship (1971).

text: The Supreme Court of India has power of:
explanation: The Supreme Court exercises original jurisdiction (disputes between states/Centre), appellate (appeals from High Courts), and advisory (President's reference) jurisdiction. [Board 2020]

text: The partition of India was decided at the:
explanation: Mountbatten Plan (also called Indian Independence Plan), June 3, 1947, announced partition into India and Pakistan. [Board 2020] Cripps Mission failed; Cabinet Mission proposed unified India; Wavell Plan never implemented.

text: India is described as a 'Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic' in:
explanation: The Preamble of the Constitution describes India's nature. These words were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976). [Board 2023] Article 1 says 'India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States'; Article 12 defines 'State'; Article 51 = international peace.

text: Which treaty ended World War I?
explanation: The Treaty of Versailles (June 28, 1919) officially ended WWI, placing sole responsibility ('war guilt') on Germany. [Board 2023] Paris 1856 ended Crimean War; Berlin 1878 = Congress of Berlin; Utrecht 1713 = Spanish Succession War.

text: The President of India addresses a joint sitting of Parliament for the first time every:
explanation: The President addresses the first joint sitting of Parliament after each general election and at the start of each budget session. [Board 2023] Not every 5 years specifically; joint sitting for bill disputes; not monthly.

text: The Swadeshi Movement (1905) mainly advocated:
options: Use of Indian goods and boycott of British goods
explanation: Swadeshi Movement promoted Indian-made goods (swadeshi) and boycott of British/foreign goods as a protest against Bengal Partition. [Board 2023] Peaceful negotiation = Moderates generally; armed resistance = later revolutionaries; foreign investment is opposite.

text: UNICEF stands for:
options: United Nations International Commerce and Finance
explanation: UNICEF = United Nations Children's Fund (formerly International Children's Emergency Fund). Works for children's rights and welfare globally. [Board 2023]

text: Directive Principles are:
explanation: Directive Principles (Part IV) are non-justiciable (cannot be enforced by courts) but fundamental in governance — state must apply them in law-making. [Board 2023] Fundamental Rights are justiciable; DPs are different from FRs; they are not optional — they guide policy.

text: The Berlin Wall fell in:
explanation: The Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989, symbolising the end of the Cold War and leading to German reunification in 1990. [Board 2023] 1961 = Berlin Wall built; 1991 = USSR dissolved; 1980 = Reagan elected (Cold War escalation).

text: The Champaran Satyagraha (1917) was Gandhi's first major non-violent movement in India against:
explanation: In Champaran (Bihar), Gandhi led farmers against British planters forcing them to grow indigo — his first major non-violent campaign in India. [Board 2023] Salt tax = Dandi (1930); Bengal Partition = Swadeshi (1905); Rowlatt Act = 1919.

text: Writ of Habeas Corpus is issued to:
options: Compel an authority to perform duty
explanation: Habeas Corpus = 'produce the body'. Issued to free a person detained unlawfully. [Board 2023] Compel duty = Mandamus; question jurisdiction = Certiorari; transfer case = is not a writ.

text: Who gave the famous speech 'Tryst with Destiny' at midnight on August 14–15, 1947?
explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru delivered the 'Tryst with Destiny' speech in the Constituent Assembly as India became independent at midnight. [Board 2023] Gandhi was not present; Patel was 'Iron Man'; Ambedkar was Constitution's architect.

text: The salaries and allowances of the ministers are decided by the:
explanation: Salaries and allowances of ministers are fixed by Parliament through law. Finance Minister proposes budget but Parliament approves; President or PM alone cannot fix ministerial salaries.

text: Civil Cases : Court of District Judge :: Criminal Cases :
explanation: Sessions Court handles serious criminal cases (equivalent to District Court for civil). Revenue courts handle land revenue; Family courts handle matrimonial disputes; Commissioner's Court handles administrative matters.

text: A house has strength 550. On a particular day 50 members are present. The Speaker decides to adjourn the house. The MOST LIKELY reason is:
explanation: Quorum for Lok Sabha is 1/10th of total membership = 55 members minimum. With only 50 present (less than 55), there's lack of quorum, requiring adjournment. Disorder or privilege breach could be reasons but the numbers point clearly to quorum.

text: During a hung assembly when no party gets majority, the President appoints PM. What power is the President exercising?
explanation: Discretionary powers allow the President to act independently without ministerial advice in special situations like a hung assembly. This is not legislative (making laws) or judicial (judging cases) or normal executive power.

text: Assertion: Forward Bloc aimed to abolish Zamindari System. Reason: Subhash Chandra Bose wanted to establish a socialist state. Which is correct?
options: A is true but R is false
R is the reason for A
Both A and R are false
Only R is true, A is false
explanation: Both statements are true and R explains A: Bose's socialist goals for India led to Forward Bloc's objective of abolishing the feudal Zamindari system. R is the ideological basis for A.

text: The ___ aimed to introduce equality between British and Indian Judges.
explanation: The Ilbert Bill (1883) proposed that Indian judges could try European (British) offenders — equality between Indian and British judges. Vernacular Press Act restricted Indian press; Gagging Act curbed free speech.

text: The Rowlatt Act was called the Black Act because Indians:
options: could be arrested without a warrant
could be sent overseas on duty
explanation: Rowlatt Act (1919) allowed detention without trial (arrest without warrant) — hence called Black Act. It suppressed political activity and was widely opposed, leading to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

text: Who organised the Grand Delhi Durbar?
explanation: Lord Curzon organised the Grand Delhi Durbar in 1903 to celebrate the coronation of Edward VII as Emperor of India. Lord Lytton organised the 1877 Durbar for Queen Victoria being declared Empress.

text: Which method would an Early Nationalist MOST LIKELY use to solve the problem of a damaged road to school?
options: Write a petition to the authorities
Block the entrance to the road
explanation: Early Nationalists (Moderates) believed in constitutional methods — writing petitions, memorials, and representations to authorities. They did not use direct action, boycott, or confrontation.

text: Which of the following objectives of INA was the ODD ONE OUT?
options: Organise provisional government of Free India
Total mobilisation of Indian manpower and money
Train and organise public opinion in the country
explanation: INA's objectives were military: form provisional government, mobilise resources, and the motto 'Unity, Faith, Sacrifice.' Training public opinion was Gandhi's Congress method, not the military INA's approach.

text: Which Indian leader's contribution must be mentioned in a speech about the Sati system in India?
explanation: Raja Rammohan Roy campaigned against Sati and was instrumental in having it banned in 1829 by Lord William Bentinck. He founded Brahmo Samaj and is called the Father of Indian Renaissance.

text: Which is NOT a consequence of the Second World War?
options: Austria and Hungary became separate states
explanation: Austria and Hungary becoming separate states was a consequence of WWI (Treaty of Saint-Germain), not WWII. WWII consequences: Axis powers defeated, Cold War started, UN formed.

text: Identify the principle of Panchsheel.
explanation: Panchsheel (1954) principles include: mutual non-aggression, mutual non-interference, peaceful coexistence, equality, mutual benefit. The other options relate to UN Charter functions, not Panchsheel.

text: Which incident depicted in the cartoon led to the beginning of the Second World War?
explanation: WWII began on September 1, 1939 when Hitler attacked Poland. Britain and France declared war on Germany 2 days later. Annexation of Austria (Anschluss) and occupation of Czechoslovakia preceded but didn't start WWII.

text: Given candidates for High Court Judge: P(65, distinguished jurist), Q(61, HC Advocate 10 yrs), R(67, HC Advocate 5 yrs), S(56, judicial officer 10 yrs). Who is eligible?
explanation: HC Judge must be: under 62 years OR qualified (HC advocate for 10+ years OR judicial officer 10+ years). Q(61, 10yr advocate) ✓; S(56, 10yr judicial) ✓; P(65) is over 62; R(67, only 5yr advocate) doesn't qualify.

text: Which event led to WWI according to the cartoon of Milton Rawson Halladay?
explanation: Germany's attack on Poland on September 1, 1939 is universally accepted as the event that triggered WWII. The cartoon depicts this invasion. Other events occurred before but didn't trigger the war's start.

text: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the:
explanation: Collective responsibility means the Council of Ministers (cabinet) is answerable to Lok Sabha. If Lok Sabha passes a vote of no confidence, the entire cabinet must resign. They are NOT responsible to Rajya Sabha.

text: Which citizen is eligible to be a member of the Rajya Sabha? W(25, journalist), X(45, industrialist), Y(35, declared insolvency), Z(50, taken citizenship of another country).
explanation: Rajya Sabha eligibility: must be 30+ years old, Indian citizen, not insolvent, not of unsound mind. X(45, industrialist) qualifies. W(25) is too young; Y(insolvency declared) is disqualified; Z(foreign citizenship) is disqualified.

text: Advisory Jurisdiction : Advise the President :: Judicial Review :
options: Review judgements of the High Court
explanation: Judicial Review is the Supreme Court's power to examine and declare laws passed by Parliament unconstitutional if they violate the Constitution. Advisory jurisdiction gives opinions to the President.

text: If an Adjournment Motion is passed in the Lok Sabha:
options: House will discuss a matter of urgent public importance
explanation: An Adjournment Motion in Lok Sabha, if admitted, provides an opportunity to discuss a matter of urgent public importance. It doesn't dissolve the house or end the session; the government falls if a No-Confidence motion passes.

text: Which emergency will be declared by President if security of the Nation is under threat?
explanation: National Emergency (General Emergency) under Article 352 is declared when security of India is threatened by war, external aggression, or armed rebellion. Financial Emergency (360) is for financial crisis; President's Rule (356) is for state government failure.

text: Assertion: Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905. Reason: The Nationalists felt that partition was to divide Hindus and Muslims. Which is correct?
options: A is true and R is false
R is true but A is false
Both A and R are independent
A is the reason for R
explanation: A is true: Curzon did partition Bengal in 1905. R is false about cause — Curzon's official reason was administrative efficiency, not divide-and-rule. However nationalists believed/suspected divide-and-rule was the motive.

text: He introduced the Subsidiary Alliance to expand British control over India.
explanation: Lord Wellesley introduced the Subsidiary Alliance (1798) — Indian rulers had to maintain British troops at their expense and accept a British Resident. Lord Dalhousie used Doctrine of Lapse; Lord Curzon used partition.

text: Identify the ODD ONE OUT among Assertive Nationalist Leaders:
explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji was an Early Nationalist (Moderate), not an Assertive (Extremist) Nationalist. Bipin Chandra Pal, Lala Lajpat Rai (the Lal Bal Pal trio), and Tilak were Assertive Nationalists.

text: Identify the contributions of Subhash Chandra Bose: P-Supreme Commander of INA, Q-Signed Lucknow Pact, R-Led Quit India Movement, S-Founded Forward Bloc.
explanation: Bose was Supreme Commander of INA (P) ✓ and founded Forward Bloc (S) ✓. Lucknow Pact (Q) was Tilak-Jinnah agreement (1916); Quit India Movement (R) was led by Gandhi (1942) while Bose was abroad.

text: A market dominated by foreign products. Local residents want to use Assertive Nationalist methods to help Indian industries. Which method should they follow?
explanation: Swadeshi movement promoted use of Indian goods and boycott of foreign goods. This is the Assertive Nationalist method to boost Indian industry. Passive resistance and national education were also Assertive methods but Swadeshi directly addresses the economic issue.

text: Which is NOT an objective of the United Nations Organisation?
explanation: The 4D objectives of UN include: Disarm (reduce weapons), Decolonise (free colonies), Develop (economic development). 'Disengage' is not a UN objective — that's more a policy of non-involvement.

text: Which agency of the UN is associated with children's welfare worldwide?
explanation: UNICEF (United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund) focuses on children's rights, nutrition, education, and healthcare globally. UNESCO is education/culture/science; WHO is health; ILO is labour standards.

text: Which is a common cause for the rise of dictatorship?
explanation: Economic crises create public desperation and disillusionment with democratic governments, making people receptive to strong authoritarian leaders. Faith in democracy, press freedom, and stability all PREVENT dictatorship.

text: Which cause of WWI is connected to the Sarajevo crisis headline?
explanation: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo (June 1914) is specifically called the Sarajevo Crisis — the immediate/direct cause of WWI. Imperialism, nationalism, and arms race were long-term/underlying causes.

text: Which emergency is declared when financial stability of India is threatened?
explanation: Financial Emergency under Article 360 is proclaimed when financial stability or credit of India (or any part) is threatened. National Emergency is for security threats; State Emergency (President's Rule) is for state governance failure.

text: The Supreme Court's power to examine constitutionality of laws passed by Parliament is called:
explanation: Judicial Review is the power to review and strike down laws inconsistent with the Constitution. Writ jurisdiction issues writs; Original jurisdiction handles certain cases directly; Appellate jurisdiction hears appeals.

text: Which jurisdiction of the High Court involves collection of State Revenue? (The word 'Consultative' in the question is to be corrected):
explanation: Original jurisdiction: HC handles revenue (tax collection disputes) matters as a court of first instance. Advisory is for President's questions; Revisory is for reviewing lower court decisions; Appellate is for hearing appeals.

text: Which session of Parliament is most associated with budget presentation?
explanation: The Budget Session (February–May) is when the Union Budget is presented and passed. Summer session is not a formal session; Winter Session (November–December) discusses general matters; Monsoon Session (July–August) handles monsoon-related legislation.

text: Who is eligible to be Vice President? W(30, army officer), X(25, union leader), Y(34, school principal), Z(69, retired professor).
explanation: VP eligibility: 35+ years, Indian citizen, qualified to be Rajya Sabha member (not Lok Sabha), not holding office of profit. Y(34) is too young, X(25) too young, W(30) is army (office of profit). Z(69, professor) qualifies — no age limit for VP.

text: President's Rule in a state is proclaimed on the recommendation of:
explanation: President's Rule (Article 356) in a state is proclaimed on the report of the Governor who recommends it to the President. President, VP, and CJI are not part of this recommendation process — Governor is the constitutional head of state.

text: Mr. Anand is illegally detained; family cannot meet him. The family approached HC. Which writ will be issued?
explanation: Habeas Corpus (meaning 'produce the body') orders the detaining authority to produce the person before court and justify the detention. Quo Warranto challenges authority; Mandamus orders performance of duty; Certiorari quashes lower court orders.

text: Identify the correct statements about the Lok Sabha: P-No nominated members, Q-Term can be extended during emergency, R-Two members nominated by President, S-Can be dissolved by Speaker.
explanation: Q is correct: Lok Sabha term can be extended by 1 year during National Emergency. R is correct: 2 Anglo-Indian members (until 2020) were nominated. P is wrong: president nominates members; S is wrong: President dissolves Lok Sabha on PM's advice, not Speaker.

text: Assertion: Hitler attacked Poland to capture the Danzig Port. Reason: Poland was accused of committing atrocities against the Germans. Which is correct?
options: A is true and R is false
A is false and R is true
Both A and R are true, R is correct explanation
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation
explanation: Both are true: A — Hitler attacked Poland, claiming Danzig (a German-speaking city/port) should be returned to Germany. R — Germany also accused Poland of mistreating ethnic Germans. R provides Hitler's justification (even if propaganda), so it is the explanation.

text: Identify the correct chronological order: 1-Lucknow Pact, 2-Surat Split, 3-Establishment of Muslim League
explanation: Muslim League founded: 1906; Surat Split: 1907; Lucknow Pact: 1916. Correct chronological order: 3(1906) → 2(1907) → 1(1916) = 3-2-1.

text: Identify the odd one out of the signatories of the Triple Entente:
explanation: The Triple Entente (1907) was formed by France, Russia, and Britain (England). Japan was allied with Britain (Anglo-Japanese Alliance) but was NOT a member of the Triple Entente.

text: Students upset about trees being cut take action based on Early Nationalist lessons. Which action are they NOT likely to adopt?
options: Forcibly prevent workers sent by Government
explanation: Early Nationalists (Moderates) used constitutional, non-violent methods: petitions, letters, peaceful demonstrations, constructive work. Forcible prevention of government workers is an aggressive/illegal action — NOT a moderate method.

text: Under which policy of British expansion was the place marked in the map annexed?
explanation: Doctrine of Lapse (Lord Dalhousie): if a ruler died without natural heir, the state would lapse to British. This was used to annex Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur, etc. Subsidiary Alliance didn't involve outright annexation; misgovernance pretext was used for Oudh.

text: Identify the correct pair: Doctrine of Lapse-Lord; Subsidiary Alliance-Lord; Arms Act-Lord; Vernacular Press Act-Lord
explanation: Subsidiary Alliance was introduced by Lord Wellesley ✓. Doctrine of Lapse was Lord Dalhousie (not Canning); Arms Act was Lord Lytton (not Curzon); Vernacular Press Act was Lord Lytton (not Dalhousie).

text: Which is NOT a consequence of the Second World War?
options: Formation of the League of Nations
explanation: The League of Nations was formed after WWI (1919, Treaty of Versailles) — NOT after WWII. WWII consequences: Axis powers defeated, Cold War began, United Nations formed (1945). The League of Nations actually collapsed during WWII.

text: He was an Early Nationalist leader who presided over the second session of the Indian National Congress.
explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji presided over the second session of INC (1886, Calcutta). W.C. Bonerjee presided over the first session (1885); Gokhale was an Early Nationalist but not second-session president; Tyabji presided over third session.

text: If the Speaker of Lok Sabha is to be removed, the resolution must be passed by:
explanation: The Speaker can be removed by a resolution passed by an absolute majority (more than 50% of total membership) of Lok Sabha. Simple majority is more than 50% of members present and voting; special majority is for constitutional amendments.

text: The Supreme Court of India exercises original jurisdiction in cases between:
explanation: Supreme Court's Original Jurisdiction (Article 131) covers disputes between: Centre and State(s), and between States. It does NOT include disputes between citizens and state (that goes to HC) or between two HCs.
